newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 25.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- PEOPLES PHONE SETTLES ACTION OVER DEPARTURE

The mobile phone service provider, Peoples Phone, is to settle a legal action with former chief executive Charles Wigoder which will allow him to exercise half of his 300,000 share options worth around 1.3 million pounds stg. Wigoder will collect almost 7 million pounds stg from the sale of his holdings in the group which is being bought by Vodafone for 77 million pounds stg.
-- SEARS TO SELL OFF FREEMANS

Sears has put its mail order division, Freemans, up for sale, with a hope that the business will fetch between 300 and 400 million pounds stg. A successful sale could help relieve pressure on chief executive Liam Strong, who is under pressure from institutional shareholders who are unhappy at the company's poor performance.
-- PLUM JOB IN SPAIN FOR BZW

BZW, Barclays Bank's investment arm, has successfully beat off strong competition from rival merchant banks to become strategic financial adviser on the preparation to a proposed US$11 billion European privatisation of Endesa, the Spanish electricity generator and distribution giant. The Spanish government's stake in Endesa, the largest utility in Spain, is expected to be sold in three tranches, starting next year and then continuing in 1998 and 1999.
THE TIMES
-- CRESTCO MAY SEEK TO RAISE EXTRA CASH TO BUY MORE TIME

CrestCo, the company responsible for the City's transfer to a paperless trading system, will have a board meeting today to decide whether to call for more money from its 60 backers to enable it to extend the Crest system's transition period beyond next April.
-- AEA WINS CHINESE NUCLEAR WORK

AEA Technology, the recently privatised nuclear waste management company, is believed to have been awarded a contract to advise staff at China's first nuclear power plant, on environmental safety. Experts from AEA are to train over 100 Chinese managers and technicians in subjects such as waste management, decommissioning reactors and environmental risks of radiation.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BT WON OVER BY ARGUMENT FOR ETHICAL AUDIT

British Telecom is set to become the first mainstream UK Business to undertake a social audit, to provide an independent assessment of its treatment of staff, customers and other stakeholders. BT's plan emerged as it published four books on its commitment to ethical and environmental action and is part of a growing movement for business to act ethically.
-- GAS COMPLAINTS MORE THAN DOUBLE

Figures released by the Gas Consumers Council show that complaints about the standards of service at British Gas have risen by more than twice the levels of last year. The figures also indicate that the increase will continue to rise over the winter months. There were 28,615 complaints registered in the first 10 months of the year by customers who had failed to have a grievance dealt with properly by British Gas Trading, which supplies gas to homes and bills customers.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- WESTCOUNTRY CHIEF POCKETS 4 MILLION POUNDS FROM BID

Stephen Redfarn, the chief executive of Westcountry Television, is to make up to 4 million pounds stg after the 85 million pounds stg bid from Carlton Communication for the South-west of England ITV franchise. The deal, which came as a surprise over the weekend, is set to re-ignite the takeover fever in the commercial television sector.
-- AT&T STEPS UP ATTACK ON BT TAKEOVER

AT&T, the US telephone giant, will today intensify its attack on the proposed takeover of MCI by British Telecom, by questioning the way the UK phone market is regulated. The company will suggest at a conference of managers of large phone networks that the market is in danger of being turned into a duopoly by BT and Cable & Wireless.
-- SUPERMARKETS BAG A GREATER SHARE OF THE DRINKS TRADE

Supermarkets have lifted their share of the take-home drinks market by 14 per cent over the last 6 years to 64 per cent. The rise is at the expense of traditional off-licenses, and is expected to grow despite planning curbs on new superstores. A new survey published by Verdict Research says that better marketing and buying power of the supermarkets will continue to win market share from specialists such as Threshers and Victoria Wine.
